claim: Drosophila melanogaster males sing a multi-part, species-specific courtship song that is both critical to female receptivity and encourages courtship by nearby males.
source: Drosophila melanogaster males sing a multi-part, species-specific courtship song that is both critical to female receptivity and encourages courtship by nearby males.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this behavioral phenomenon.

claim: fruM is expressed only in neurons, including ∼2% of neurons within the CNS, as well as sensory, motor, and higher-order interneurons.
source: In contrast, fruM is expressed only in neurons, including ∼2% of neurons within the CNS, as well as sensory, motor, and higher-order interneurons, all of which might comprise neural circuits dedicated to sexual behaviors (Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Manoli et al., 2005 and Stockinger et al., 2005.

claim: Courtship song consists of two parts: a rhythmic pulse song with an ∼35-ms inter-pulse interval (IPI) and a ∼160-Hz sine song.
source: When courting a female, the male vibrates his wing to generate a courtship song consisting of two parts: a rhythmic pulse song with an ∼35-ms inter-pulse interval (IPI) that strongly elicits male courtship behavior as well as female receptivity, as well as a ∼160-Hz sine song that may play a secondary role (Shorey, 1962; Bennet-Clark and Ewing, 1967; von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Arthur et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Shorey, 1962; Bennet-Clark and Ewing, 1967; von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Arthur et al., 2013).

claim: Pulse song with ∼35 ms IPI strongly elicits male courtship behavior as well as female receptivity.
source: When courting a female, the male vibrates his wing to generate a courtship song consisting of two parts: a rhythmic pulse song with an ∼35-ms inter-pulse interval (IPI) that strongly elicits male courtship behavior as well as female receptivity, as well as a ∼160-Hz sine song that may play a secondary role (Shorey, 1962; Bennet-Clark and Ewing, 1967; von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Arthur et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Drosophila receives sound stimuli by vibration of the arista, a feather-like structure protruding from the second segment of the antenna.
source: Drosophila receives sound stimuli by vibration of the arista, a feather-like structure protruding from the second segment of the antenna (Gopfert and Robert, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gopfert and Robert, 2001.

claim: aPN1 is necessary for both female receptivity and the male song-induced locomotion response.
source: aPN1 is necessary for both female receptivity and the male song-induced locomotion response, and it shows a response to courtship song that is proportional to pulse rate (Vaughan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Vaughan et al., 2014.

claim: Female pC1 neurons are activated by the male-specific pheromone cVA.
source: Female pC1 neurons are activated by the male-specific pheromone cVA (Zhou et al., 2014), while male fruM+/dsx+ P1 neurons (a subset of the dsx+ pC1 population) are inhibited by cVA but activated by female pheromones (Kohatsu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2014.

claim: Male fruM+/dsx+ P1 neurons are inhibited by cVA but activated by female pheromones.
source: Female pC1 neurons are activated by the male-specific pheromone cVA (Zhou et al., 2014), while male fruM+/dsx+ P1 neurons (a subset of the dsx+ pC1 population) are inhibited by cVA but activated by female pheromones (Kohatsu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kohatsu et al., 2011.

claim: Female pC1 neurons are also activated by sine and pulse songs.
source: Female pC1 neurons are also activated by sine and pulse songs (Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2014.

claim: Three independent GAL4 lines (R21B12, R22B11, and R49F09) label four to five aPN1 cells per hemisphere when intersected with fruLexA.
source: To characterize fruM+ aPN1 cells, we identified GAL4 drivers (R21B12, R22B11, and R49F09) that label four to five aPN1 cells per hemisphere when intersected with fruLexA (Figure 1A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Two GAL4 drivers (R72E10 and R46F09) label a subset of the fruM+ aSP-k cell type when crossed to LexAop2-FLP; fruLexA, UAS>stop>myr::GFP.
source: Two GAL4 drivers (R72E10 and R46F09) were identified that, when crossed to LexAop2-FLP; fruLexA, UAS>stop>myr::GFP, labeled a subset of the fruM+ aSP-k cell type previously identified via MARCM (Mosaic analysis with a repressible cell marker) clones (Cachero et al., 2010) (Figure 1B and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—source data 1, and citation to Cachero et al., 2010.

claim: vPN1 neurons have cell bodies located laterally in the dorsal anterior brain and neurites that innervate the WED and the LPC.
source: These neurons, termed vPN1, have cell bodies located laterally in the dorsal anterior brain and neurites that innervate the WED and the LPC (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Co-registration of fruM+ aPN1 and vPN1 neurons revealed substantial overlap in the WED region.
source: Co-registration of fruM+ aPN1 and vPN1 neurons revealed substantial overlap in the WED region (Figure 1C), suggesting potential synaptic connectivity between aPN1 and vPN1 neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: aPN1 neurons had indistinguishable projection patterns in female and male brains.
source: aPN1 neurons had indistinguishable projection patterns in female and male brains (Figure 1D–F), while vPN1 neurons were only observed in male brains (Figure 1G), with female brains showing only very weak expression in a few seemingly unrelated neurons (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 1D–F.

claim: vPN1 neurons were only observed in male brains.
source: aPN1 neurons had indistinguishable projection patterns in female and male brains (Figure 1D–F), while vPN1 neurons were only observed in male brains (Figure 1G), with female brains showing only very weak expression in a few seemingly unrelated neurons (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 1G–I.

claim: vPN1 neurons remain absent from the female brain using the vPN1 split-GAL4 driver.
source: Using this driver, vPN1 neurons remain absent from the female brain, and fruM is expressed in all vPN1 cells of the male (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: fruM is expressed in all vPN1 cells of the male.
source: Using this driver, vPN1 neurons remain absent from the female brain, and fruM is expressed in all vPN1 cells of the male (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: The male-specific expression pattern of vPN1 is not affected in heterozygous fru mutants (fru4–40/+).
source: The male-specific expression pattern of vPN1 is not affected in heterozygous fru mutants (fru4–40/+, Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: vPN1 expression is absent in fru null mutant males (fru4–40/fruLexA).
source: However, vPN1 expression is absent in fru null mutant males (fru4–40/fruLexA, Figure 2E), while misexpression of FruM protein in females (fruM/+) leads to an induction of vPN1 expression in the female brain (Figure 2F) (Demir and Dickson, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Misexpression of FruM protein in females (fruM/+) leads to an induction of vPN1 expression in the female brain.
source: However, vPN1 expression is absent in fru null mutant males (fru4–40/fruLexA, Figure 2E), while misexpression of FruM protein in females (fruM/+) leads to an induction of vPN1 expression in the female brain (Figure 2F) (Demir and Dickson, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 2F and citation to Demir and Dickson, 2005.

claim: fruM plays an instructive role in the specification of sexual dimorphism of vPN1 neurons.
source: Thus, fruM plays an instructive role in the specification of sexual dimorphism of vPN1 neurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the genetic manipulation experiments showing that fruM is necessary and sufficient for vPN1 expression.

claim: Male flies respond to courtship song by increasing locomotion and exploratory courtship of nearby flies.
source: Male flies respond to courtship song, and pulse song in particular, by increasing locomotion and exploratory courtship of nearby flies (Schilcher, 1976b; Eberl et al., 1997; Kowalski et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Male flies displayed robust song-induced chaining behavior upon stimulation by pulse song with a ramping intensity.
source: Upon stimulation by pulse song with a ramping intensity, we indeed observed that male flies displayed robust song-induced chaining behavior (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The chaining response was significantly higher for songs at 35-ms IPI than for all other IPIs, across a wide range of intensities (p < 0.05, 72.5–85 dB).
source: Indeed, the chaining response was significantly higher for songs at 35-ms IPI than for all other IPIs, across a wide range of intensities (p < 0.05, 72.5–85 dB, Wilcoxon rank-sum test; Figure 3B,C), suggesting that D. melanogaster males to some extent are able to preferentially respond to pulse song of their own species.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3B,C with statistical analysis.

claim: Silencing fruM+ aPN1 neurons reduced song-induced chaining compared to controls.
source: Three independent GAL4 ∩ fruLexA genotypes were used to confirm that silencing fruM+ aPN1 neurons reduced male courtship hearing; indeed, flies expressing tetanus neurotoxin light chain (TNT), which blocks synaptic vesicle release, in fruM+ aPN1 neurons showed significantly reduced chaining compared to controls expressing an inactive form of TNT (TNTin) or lacking fruLexA (Figure 4A–C) (Sweeney et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: fruM+ aPN1 neurons are required for song-induced male chaining.
source: Thus, fruM+ aPN1 neurons are required for song-induced male chaining.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the silencing experiments showing reduced chaining behavior.

claim: vPN1 silencing reduced song-induced chaining.
source: Using two GAL4 drivers (R72E10, R46F09) in an intersectional approach (GAL4 ∩ fruLexA) to target TNT expression to vPN1 neurons, we observed that vPN1 silencing reduced song-induced chaining (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: Both fruM+ aPN1 and fruM+ vPN1 neurons are required for the male-chaining response to pulse song.
source: As the multiple drivers used for aPN1 and vPN1 share no off-target expression in fruLexA+ neurons (Figure 4A–E), we conclude that both fruM+ aPN1 and fruM+ vPN1 fruM neurons are required for the male-chaining response to pulse song.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the silencing experiments with multiple independent drivers.

claim: vPN1 neurons respond to both pulse song and sine song, but not to white noise stimuli at 80 dB.
source: When auditory stimuli were presented at 80 dB, vPN1 neurons responded to both pulse song and sine song, but not to white noise stimuli (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: The threshold of vPN1 activation matched the behavioral threshold for song-induced chaining (EC50 = 68.2 dB for vPN1 responses v.s. EC50 = 70.6 dB for chaining responses).
source: Strikingly, the threshold of vPN1 activation matched the behavioral threshold for song-induced chaining (EC50 = 68.2 dB for vPN1 responses v.s. EC50 = 70.6 dB for chaining responses, half-maximal sigmoid fit; Figure 5F and Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5F and behavioral data in Figure 3B.

claim: vPN1 neurons respond strongly to pulse trains with IPIs of 35 ms and above, with significant attenuation at IPIs below 25 ms (p < 0.01 when compared to responses at 35-ms IPI).
source: We found that vPN1 neurons respond strongly to pulse trains with IPIs of 35 ms and above, with significant attenuation at IPIs below 25 ms (p < 0.01 when compared to responses at 35-ms IPI, Wilcoxon signed-rank test; Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 with statistical analysis.

claim: The vPN1 signal displays low-pass response properties for IPI with a shoulder around 35-ms.
source: This signal displays low-pass response properties for IPI with a shoulder around 35-ms and is different from the aPN1 response that responds as a function of pulse rate (Vaughan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the calcium imaging data and comparison to aPN1 responses.

claim: The neurites of pC1 and vPN1 neurons extensively overlap in the LPC.
source: The neurites of pC1 and vPN1 neurons extensively overlap in the LPC, including the lateral crescent, the lateral junction, the arch and the ring region (Yu et al., 2010), suggesting potential synaptic contacts between these two cell types (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6B–D and citation to Yu et al., 2010.

claim: TNT-mediated inactivation of pC1 neurons almost completely abolished song-induced chaining behavior.
source: Compared to controls, TNT-mediated inactivation of pC1 neurons almost completely abolished song-induced chaining behavior (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: pC1 neurons are only sensitive to pulse song stimuli at 80 dB and above (EC50 = 79.7 dB).
source: pC1 neurons are only sensitive to pulse song stimuli at 80 dB and above (EC50 = 79.7 dB, sigmoid fit; Figure 6I),a higher activation threshold than that observed for vPN1 (EC50 = 68.2 dB; Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Pulse-song stimuli evoked calcium transients in pC1 neurites, while sine song and white noise induced little response.
source: As expected, pulse-song stimuli evoked calcium transients in pC1 neurites, while sine song and white noise induced little response (Figure 6H), consistent with the report that sine song and white noise are not capable of inducing chaining behavior (Eberl et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6H and citation to Eberl et al., 1997.

claim: The pC1 neurite response showed a strong response to pulse song with IPIs of 35–65 ms, significantly reduced at both short (15–25 ms) and long (85–95 ms) IPIs (p < 0.01 when compared to responses at 35-ms IPI).
source: Unlike the low-pass response of vPN1, the pC1 neurite response showed a strong response to pulse song with IPIs of 35–65 ms. This response is significantly reduced at both short (15–25 ms) and long (85–95 ms) IPIs (p < 0.01 when compared to responses at 35-ms IPI, Wilcoxon signed-rank test; Figure 6K, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6K and Figure 6—figure supplement 1 with statistical analysis.

claim: The pC1 response reflects a band-pass sensitivity to pulse song.
source: This response reflects a band-pass sensitivity to pulse song, which is not seen in either aPN1 or vPN1, and qualitatively matches the IPI sensitivity of the behavioral response in male and female flies (Bennet-Clark, 1969; Yoon et al., 2013; Vaughan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the calcium imaging data and comparison to behavioral responses, supported by citations.

claim: For vPN1, there is only a moderate correlation between calcium response and the IPI sensitivity of song-induced chaining (r = 0.67; p < 0.017).
source: For vPN1, we observed only a moderate correlation between this calcium response and the IPI sensitivity of song-induced chaining (r = 0.67; p < 0.017, permutation test, Figure 6L).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of calcium imaging and behavioral data shown in Figure 6L.

claim: The pC1 response closely matches the IPI sensitivity of song-induced chaining (r = 0.89; p < 0.001).
source: In contrast, the pC1 response closely matches the IPI sensitivity of song-induced chaining (r = 0.89; p < 0.001, permutation test, Figure 6M).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of calcium imaging and behavioral data shown in Figure 6M.

claim: The correlation with the behavioral response is higher for pC1 than vPN1 (p < 0.037).
source: The correlation with the behavioral response is higher for pC1 than vPN1 (p < 0.037, Meng's z-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of correlations.

claim: pC1 activity may integrate information from vPN1 and other neurons to determine the level of courtship-chaining behavior.
source: These results suggest that pC1 activity may integrate information from vPN1 and other neurons to determine the level of courtship-chaining behavior.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation analysis and physiological data.

claim: CsChrimson-mediated activation of aPN1 neurons did not induce male-chaining behavior when tested with two independent GAL4 drivers (R22B11 and R49F09).
source: CsChrimson-mediated activation of aPN1 neurons did not induce male-chaining behavior when we tested two independent GAL4 drivers (R22B11 and R49F09) (Figure 7A,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic behavioral data shown in Figure 7A,D.

claim: CsChrimson-mediated activation of vPN1 neurons induced robust chaining behavior.
source: In contrast, CsChrimson-mediated activation of putative third-order vPN1 neurons induced robust chaining behavior (Figure 7B,D and Video 1), which was not observed in the absence of red light stimulation or in control flies lacking GAL4 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic behavioral data shown in Figure 7B,D and Video 1.

claim: Activation of pC1 neurons induced robust male-chaining behavior.
source: Similarly, activation of pC1 neurons induced robust male-chaining behavior (Figure 7C,E and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic behavioral data shown in Figure 7C,E and Video 2.

claim: Activation of vPN1 induced chaining in an intensity-dependent or frequency-dependent manner.
source: While activation of vPN1 induced chaining in an intensity-dependent or frequency-dependent manner, activation of pC1 generated a saturating response in which even the lowest intensity (0.006 mW/mm2) or the lowest frequency (10 Hz) was able to induce robust chaining through >90% of the testing period.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic behavioral data shown in Figure 7F,G.

claim: Activation of pC1 generated a saturating response in which even the lowest intensity (0.006 mW/mm2) or the lowest frequency (10 Hz) was able to induce robust chaining through >90% of the testing period.
source: While activation of vPN1 induced chaining in an intensity-dependent or frequency-dependent manner, activation of pC1 generated a saturating response in which even the lowest intensity (0.006 mW/mm2) or the lowest frequency (10 Hz) was able to induce robust chaining through >90% of the testing period.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic behavioral data shown in Figure 7F,G.

claim: The dendrites of vPN1 target the WED region, and vPN1 axonal termini ramify extensively in the LPC region.
source: The dendrites of vPN1 target the WED region, and vPN1 axonal termini ramify extensively in the LPC region (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data using DenMark and Syt::GFP shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Both dendrites and axons of pC1 are observed within the LPC region.
source: Both dendrites and axons of pC1 are observed within the LPC region (Figure 8B), and vPN1 axons overlap with pC1 dendrites when registered in a standard brain (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data using DenMark and Syt::GFP shown in Figure 8B.

claim: vPN1 axons overlap with pC1 dendrites when registered in a standard brain.
source: Both dendrites and axons of pC1 are observed within the LPC region (Figure 8B), and vPN1 axons overlap with pC1 dendrites when registered in a standard brain (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Pre-synaptic activation of aPN1 elicited calcium responses in vPN1.
source: Pre-synaptic activation of aPN1 elicited calcium responses in vPN1 (Figure 8D), suggesting a functional connection between aPN1 and vPN1.
evidence: This claim is supported by simultaneous optogenetic activation and calcium imaging data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Activation of vPN1 elicited robust calcium responses in pC1 neurites.
source: As anticipated, activation of vPN1 elicited robust calcium responses in pC1 neurites (Figure 8E), supporting the idea that vPN1 neurons form functional synapses with pC1 neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by simultaneous optogenetic activation and calcium imaging data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The effects of aPN1 activation on vPN1 and vPN1 activation on pC1 were reduced by the administration of the acetylcholine receptor antagonist mecamylamine.
source: In both cases, these effects were reduced by the administration of the acetylcholine receptor antagonist mecamylamine (Figure 8D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacology experiments shown in Figure 8D,E.

claim: Significant GRASP signal was observed in the WED region between aPN1 and vPN1 neurons.
source: By expressing spGFP11 in aPN1 neurons and spGFP1-10 in vPN1 neurons, we observed significant GRASP signal in the WED region (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D), suggesting the connections between aPN1 and vPN1.
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: No GRASP signal was detected between vPN1 neurons and pC1 neurons.
source: However, no GRASP signal was detected when we drove spGFP1-10 expression in vPN1 neurons with 72E10-GAL4 and spGFP11 expression in pC1 neurons with 71G01-LexA (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRASP data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The aPN1-vPN1-pC1 pathway is a labeled line for courtship hearing.
source: We have demonstrated that the aPN1-vPN1-pC1 pathway is a labeled line for courtship hearing, by fulfilling four criteria: (1) these neurons are functionally connected; (2) these neurons respond preferentially to courtship song; (3) these neurons are necessary for the behavioral response to courtship song in male flies, and (4) activation of this labeled line provides a fictive stimulus, observable by the chaining response elicited upon CsChrimson activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined anatomical, behavioral, and physiological evidence presented in the study.

claim: vPN1 may represent the third-order auditory neurons.
source: We present several lines of evidence suggesting that vPN1 may represent the third-order auditory neurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the anatomical, behavioral, and physiological evidence presented.

claim: vPN1 neurons likely target dsx+ pC1 neurons directly.
source: In addition, we found that vPN1 neurons likely target dsx+ pC1 neurons directly.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the anatomical overlap and functional connectivity data.

claim: The aPN1-vPN1-pC1 pathway provides a labeled line for processing courtship song in Drosophila.
source: Taken together, we provide anatomical, behavioral, and physiological evidence that the aPN1-vPN1-pC1 pathway provides a labeled line for processing courtship song in Drosophila.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined evidence presented in the study.

claim: The vPN1 population constitutes a male-specific subset of the larger aSP-k cell type.
source: We therefore infer that the vPN1 population constitutes a male-specific subset of the larger aSP-k cell type.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the anatomical and genetic data showing male-specific expression.

claim: The IPI sensitivity appropriate for species-appropriate responses is likely to be generated through a multi-stage transformation of song stimuli.
source: Thus, while the mechanistic details remain unclear, the IPI sensitivity appropriate for species-appropriate responses is likely to be generated through a multi-stage transformation of song stimuli.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of IPI tuning across aPN1, vPN1, and pC1.

claim: pC1 neurons are sexually dimorphic in both cell number and morphology.
source: The central integrators of courtship-related sensory cues in male and female flies, the pC1 neurons, are themselves sexually dimorphic in both cell number and morphology (Kimura et al., 2008; Kohatsu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: pC1 neurons show male-specific innervation of the LPC arch and male-specific contralateral projections.
source: pC1 neurons arborize within the triangular lateral junction of the LPC in both sexes, where integration of multiple sensory modalities may occur, but they also show male-specific innervation of the LPC arch and male-specific contralateral projections (Kimura et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: pC1 neurons are stimulated by pulse song in both sexes, but are also stimulated by sine song in females.
source: For courtship hearing, pC1 neurons are stimulated by pulse song in both sexes, but are also stimulated by sine song in females (Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2014.

claim: Both males and females are responsive to pulse song, while females are also responsive to sine song.
source: This result is consistent with the behavioral observation that both males and females are responsive to pulse song, while females are also responsive to sine song (Bennet-Clark, 1969; Schilcher, 1976a, 1976b; Eberl et al., 1997; Shirangi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: aSP-k neurons are present in both sexes and extend male-specific processes that innervate the LPC arch.
source: However, aSP-k neurons are present in both sexes and extend male-specific processes that innervate the LPC arch (Cachero et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cachero et al., 2010.

claim: There is a gradient of sexual dimorphism across the ascending pathway for both olfaction and audition, with limited dimorphism in second-order neurons but dramatic changes in third-order neurons and integrative neurons.
source: More generally, we observe a gradient of sexual dimorphism across the ascending pathway for both olfaction and audition. In both cases, we note only limited sexual dimorphism in second-order neurons (DA1 and aPN1, respectively), but dramatic changes in third-order neurons (aSP-f/aSP-g and vPN1) and integrative neurons (pC1), which show significant dimorphisms in cell number and morphology (Datta et al., 2008; Ruta et al., 2010; Kohatsu et al., 2011; Kohl et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of sexual dimorphism across different neuron types, supported by citations.
